input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Warranty period: ninety days = 90 days (i.e., 3 months), running from the later of delivery or acceptance, so the period is at least 90 days and meets the preferred threshold; the automated check failed only because Section 19.2 spells the number out in words ("ninety days") rather than using a numeral or a months/years form, which is a false negative and not a substantive shortfall. On substance Section 19 sits at or above the preferred position: 19.1 warrants Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel to industry standards plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives the 90-day (3-month) Deliverable conformance warranty and warrants Hosted Services will conform throughout the entire subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark for a hosted product; 19.3 adds no-malicious-code, Applicable Law compliance, no functionality diminishment and no contaminating open source. The remedy in 19.4 is prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid, and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims, satisfying the repair/replace/refund requirement. The disclaimer in 19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty and "AS IS" walk-away territory is not implicated. Section 6 acceptance testing does not truncate the warranty (the period runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, and 6.2 adds an independent correction, termination and refund path) and Section 3.1 reinforces the performance standard. No redline is warranted; the only observation is the drafting nit that "ninety days" could be written "ninety (90) days" for machine readability.
